extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating multilingual speech representation learning, covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is a benchmark assembled from existing publicly available multilingual speech datasets (FLEURS, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) covering 102 languages across 4 task families. Unlabeled speech is available through corpora already used in past work (e.g. MLS, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice). Scripts are provided to download and reproduce preprocessing steps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of read speech and other speech domains from existing datasets: FLEURS (102 languages, read-speech), MLS (8 languages, read-speech), VoxPopuli (14 languages, Euro Parliament speech), CoVoST-2 (21 language pairs, speech translation), Minds-14 (14 languages, e-banking intent), and Common Crawl text data (mC4 dataset).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 annotation per item for most tasks, 1 or 5 for speech retrieval (FLEURS mining task)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may have imbalanced representation across language families, with a noted gap between various language families or groups.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Speech data is not abundant for all languages; the benchmark covers a few-shot/low-resource setting. Training sets range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language. Test sets are open to the public rather than hidden.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to make speech technology available in all languages, giving speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and enabling their content and culture to be known outside their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluation (benchmarking) of multilingual speech representation learning, covering tasks including speech recognition, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval. It also supports pre-training, fine-tuning, self-training, and language model development. Guidelines specify that only task-specific ASR supervision should be used at fine-tuning time, and that text data for classification tasks can be used at training but not inference time.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The datasets and tasks are open-sourced and made easily accessible. Scripts are provided to download and reproduce preprocessing steps. Submissions are encouraged to use publicly available datasets, and new filtering techniques or data should be released in open-source when possible.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: TTS augmentation and self-training are encouraged; additional unlabeled speech data can be used for pre-training, self-training, and TTS-augmented data; text-to-text machine translation data can be used for speech translation with TTS systems to augment training sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering of unlabeled text data is encouraged; hyperparameter search and checkpoint selection performed on dev set; test set predictions submitted for double-checking; language modeling decoding results reported with and without LM fusion.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S, a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Unlabeled speech is available publicly through corpora already used in past work (e.g. MLS, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice)... When needed, we provide scripts to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Unlabeled speech is available publicly through corpora already used in past work (e.g. MLS, VoxPopuli, CommonVoice)... Tasks have also been selected based on their usage by pre-existing multilingual pre-trained models, for simplicity.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: FLEURS 999h ... Read-speech; MLS 80h ... Read-speech; VoxPopuli 1300h ... Euro Parl; CoVoST-2 566h ... ; Minds-14 2h ... E-banking. Unlabeled text data is available in all languages, for instance, through Common Crawl data as in the mC4 dataset.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We specify the type of fine-tuning (monolingual or multilingual), which coincides with the number of fine-tuning runs... Either 1/5 [for FLEURS speech retrieval]

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We believe there remains significant room for improvements on those tasks, in particular when it comes to reducing the gap between various language families or groups.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Speech data is however not abundant for all languages, so multilinguality is important to build strong representations for those languages. The training sets of XTREME-S range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language. This is a few-shot setting suited for low-resource understanding.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: XTREME-S is meant to be a more exhaustive, thorough and complete evaluation of learned speech representations. It covers 102 diverse languages... and includes four different task families: recognition, translation, classification and retrieval... We ask that submissions leverage only the ASR supervision of each task... The text data of each task can be used at training time but not at inference time.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Tasks are all directly open-sourced and made easily accessible... Each task should be available under a permissive license that allows the use and redistribution of the data for research purposes. When needed, we provide scripts to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps... the technique should be explained clearly and the data released in open-source when possible.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We do encourage submissions that also use different unlabeled speech, although preferably only in the case where there is a substantial difference (e.g. much smaller or much larger, or from more diverse sources, or using TTS-augmented data etc). Additional unlabeled speech data can be used for pre-training but also for self-training and other methods.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We hope the community can also develop smarter ways to adapt these very large unlabeled text datasets to each particular task and domain through filtering methods... We trust practitioners to perform all hyperparameter search and checkpoint selection on the dev set, and eventually report performance on the test set. Results are however double-checked through the submission of the predictions of the model for each task.
